scope: Continuation review of the cd4336e comparison fixes and the phase-power model. All authoritative checks rerun from a git archive of cb2d280 after concurrent industrial-case edits were detected. Those concurrent edits are excluded.
accepted_progress: Ordinary missing-point and case-subset paths now report incomplete. Published complete cases have six rows and no failure flags. The v2 result is incomplete, six of seven complete-case wins in each model.

findings.problem: completeness() derives complete from the old legal FV rows without subtracting failed labels, while compare() filters explicit failed labels for scoring. These two sets can disagree. train_failed is also not applied to the scoring filter.
findings.trigger: Retry placements after exporting FV results, then combine the newer timing.json with the previous FV JSON.

evidence.protocol: Actual compare(), ten cases. Old FV JSON has six legal rows; newer timing marks five labels failed; only the surviving WL score exists.

findings.recommendation: Resolve one authoritative current successful-label set, with explicit and training failures taking precedence, and use it for scoring, completeness and counts. Reject contradictory stale inputs or report them incomplete.

findings.problem: A valid failed or wholly illegal case can have zero scored ATPlace points; outcome() divides by zero before the new incomplete verdict can be emitted.

evidence.protocol: Actual compare() with no legal ATPlace point and all six labels marked failed.

findings.recommendation: Represent zero-score outcomes as unavailable with null ratios, retain failure counts and emit an incomplete report without treating failure as either win or loss.

findings.problem: The timestamp fix covers a locally rewritten layout but not changed scoring configuration or changed content copied with a preserved timestamp. A score newer than a file does not prove it scores that content/configuration.

evidence.protocol: Actual score_only file handling; scoring subprocess stub returns a number identifying the supplied configuration. Layout unchanged, params changed between invocations.

preserved_mtime_control.protocol: Changed layout bytes with original mtime preserved (copy2/rsync -t behavior).

findings.recommendation: Bind cached scores to layout bytes and relevant resolved evaluation configuration/version, or always rescore in a fresh immutable run directory. Do not certify historical score-layout identity solely from mtimes.

method_analysis.question: Can the current three phase powers create a different worst-mode robust placement problem?
method_analysis.derivation: For fixed L and phase-invariant thermal system, theta(L,p)=G(L)^(-1) B(L) p. Nonnegative conductances with heat paths give inverse-positive G, and B is nonnegative. Since p_prefill >= p_decode >= p_idle componentwise, every node and per-die peak follows that order. With common per-die limits, J_robust(L)=J_prefill(L) for every supported L.
method_analysis.consequence: Multi-mode worst-overshoot search cannot add a tradeoff over prefill alone for these powers. A change in the identity of the die with the least margin does not change this result. Prune componentwise-dominated powers before costly robust search; incomparable powers are necessary but not sufficient for a useful multi-mode layout tradeoff.
method_analysis.distinction: This does not prove that optimizing each phase separately yields the same layouts. It proves equality of the joint worst-mode objective and the prefill-only objective under the stated model.

evidence.protocol: Three legal layouts, fixed saved h=7280.435855771514 W/m2K, resolution64, real FV for each of three phases. No fit repeated.
conditions: same layout-dependent conductance matrix and source map in every phase
nonnegative conductances with ambient heat path, thus inverse-positive thermal operator
fixed ambient, cooling and per-die limits across phases; no temperature-dependent power
evidence.conclusion: For every supported layout L, J_robust(L)=J_prefill(L). The numerical examples illustrate the analytic monotonicity result, not an exhaustive empirical proof.

limits: Comparison controls use synthetic scores and deterministic external-process stubs; no real ATSim invocation or remote job was performed.
Published complete-case counts do not exhibit the contradictory-failure control. No published six-of-seven result is shown wrong by these controls.
The phase diagnostic uses three real FV layouts with an existing saved h; it is not a new cooling calibration. The all-layout result comes from monotonicity under the explicit assumptions.
No external thermal validation or real timing validation was performed; currently edited industrial-case files are outside this snapshot review.
